summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Q1 (documented sectoral damage functions for Nepal or comparable Himalayan economies) is PENDING: no document could be downloaded. A sectoral damage-function framework is defined for farming (crop yield response to temperature/precipitation plus event losses), ecosystems (area-weighted service loss, reported as welfare not GDP), hydropower (plant-level flow-generation transfer function aligned with 22D, plus hazard expected annual damage), tourism (seasonal arrivals-and-spend exposure with disruption days and amenity change) and livelihoods (asset-loss to well-being-loss by quintile), with an aggregate macro damage function as cross-check only. Each lists the functional form, the parameters needed, the candidate studies and lead ids. All ranges are carried as low/high bounds by scenario, horizon and adaptation assumption, with no point estimates. The single allowed web search located the World Bank Nepal CCDR (2022) records; other leads are reused from upstream findings and source_leads.json; ten leads are URLs from general knowledge and are marked unverified.

findings.claim: Sectoral damage parameters are carried as low/high bounds per scenario, horizon and adaptation assumption; no central value or probability distribution is assigned without evidence, and propagation uses envelope (corner) combinations rather than Monte Carlo with invented distributions.

Sectoral damages enter GDP only through the value added of the affected sector; ecosystem and livelihood losses are reported under welfare objectives and not netted into GDP; aggregate macro damage functions are a cross-check only, never added to sectoral sums.

Where sources disagree (e.g. CCDR vs ADB 2014 vs IDS-Nepal 2014), both ranges are retained with model type, climate scenario generation (CMIP5/CMIP6), baseline year, price basis and adaptation assumption recorded.

data_gaps: No lead downloaded; all damage parameters pending.
Unknown whether the CCDR publishes sector-level coefficients or only macro outputs; background papers must be checked.
No Nepal-specific tourism or ecosystem-service damage function located; these may remain qualitative.

IDS-Nepal/PAC/GCAP (2014) Nepal economic impact study, MoFE NAP (2021) and Climate Change Scenarios for Nepal (2019), NLSS IV and MoALD statistics have no verified document URLs (general knowledge only).
Comparable Himalayan-economy studies (Bhutan, Pakistan CCDRs; Indian Himalayan states) not located.
Plant-level hydropower head/design-discharge data needed for the flow-generation function not located (shared gap with 22D).
Hazard frequency-loss curves need BIPAD event data, which is not downloadable in this environment.

assumptions.text: Ranges are scenario-conditional low/high bounds; no probabilities or central values are assigned without evidence; scenarios are stress tests, not forecasts.
Damage fractions apply to sector gross value added in Nepal FY; climate horizons are calendar/multi-decade; conversions happen only at the scenario-parameter interface with documented mapping.
Slow-onset (trend) and event (hazard) channels are estimated separately per sector and summed only after a double-counting check.
Money-denominated parameters keep their source price basis (current vs constant, base year) and are converted with deflators, not exchange rates alone.

challenges.text: Hydropower paths should use SIR-HY-1 (flow-transfer plus hazard EAD) with ranges from 25A PR-05/PR-07 when retrieved, not a stationary-flow assumption.
Agricultural projections should carry crop- and zone-specific yield-response bounds (SIR-AG-1) and keep CO2-fertilisation and irrigation assumptions explicit.
Ecosystem and livelihood losses (SIR-EC-1, SIR-LV-1) should be reported under welfare objectives, not netted against GDP; macro damage functions are cross-checks only.
22D and 25E share the hydropower flow-generation design; propose that 22D own plant-level calibration and 25E own hazard EAD to avoid double counting.
Catalog has no source ids for MoFE (climate scenarios, NAP) or MoALD (agricultural statistics), nor for the IDS-Nepal 2014 study (currently tagged academic); request ids and verified URLs.

uncertainty: Very high. Structural uncertainty in damage-function form (level vs growth, reduced-form vs process models), climate-scenario spread (especially monsoon precipitation), adaptation assumptions, and benefit-transfer valuation for ecosystems. Nepal-specific quantified evidence is thin outside the CCDR; tourism and ecosystem channels may remain qualitative. No values recorded.

sectoral_impact_ranges.method: Per sector: define functional form, list required parameters with low/high placeholders, map each to candidate studies and lead ids; on retrieval, extract ranges by scenario x horizon x adaptation, record each as an observation, keep conflicting sources side by side.
sectoral_impact_ranges.range_convention: low/high bounds only; central values not carried; no probability weights; propagation by envelope combinations; unit codes from src/economic_model/units.py

sectors.functional_form: Crop-specific yield response to temperature, precipitation and CO2 (reduced-form or crop-model emulator), plus separate flood/drought event-loss term
sectors.equation: dY_c,z/Y_c,z = b1_c,z*dT + b2_c,z*dT^2 + b3_c,z*dP + b4_c*dCO2 (or degree-day piecewise-linear form); dVA_ag = VA_ag,base * sum_c w_c * dY_c/Y_c (adjusted for irrigation share) - EAD_ag(flood, drought)

parameters.description: per degree C; quadratic or degree-day form

parameters.description: per percent change in seasonal rainfall

parameters.name: irrigation dampening factor
parameters.description: share of damage avoided on irrigated area

parameters.name: crop value-added weights w_c
parameters.description: crop shares of agricultural value added (Nepal FY)

parameters.name: annual expected flood/drought crop loss EAD_ag
parameters.description: percent of agricultural VA, from event-loss curve

sectors.equation: dESV = sum_k A_k * v_k * f_k(dT, dP); market part dVA_forestry = VA_forestry,base * g(dT) ; non-market part reported under the environmental objective in src/economic_model/welfare.py

sectors.methodological_notes: Benefit-transfer values are highly uncertain and not additive to GDP; ecosystem losses are reported as a separate objective, not netted against GDP gains. Most sources are qualitative for Nepal; a quantified range may not exist and must then stay pending.

sectors.functional_form: Plant-level flow-generation transfer function (run-of-river capped by installed capacity) driven by seasonal runoff change, plus hazard expected-annual-damage and outage term
